company.name: GrooveBook
company.one_liner: An app that mails you a printed book of 100 phone photos every month for $2.99.

facts.summary: A subscription app: pick up to 100 photos from your phone each month and get them printed in a perforated photo book, shipped for $2.99.
highlights: $2.99 a month for a printed book of up to 100 photos.
The founders already own a print shop, which keeps printing costs low.
Subscription revenue is recurring and predictable.
Most people never print the photos on their phones; that's the opportunity.

real_deal.summary: Mark Cuban and Kevin O'Leary teamed up on a $150,000 deal tied to licensing the service.

outcome.headline: Acquired by Shutterfly for $14.5M within a year.
outcome.story: After the episode GrooveBook signed up a huge number of subscribers, and in November 2014 Shutterfly bought the company for $14.5M. A fast exit at a modest price, but a great multiple for early investors.
